title: Geometric inverse image from the profinite point and its monoidal comparisons
statement:
Choose universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathbf{Prof}$ be the category of compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces and continuous maps in the smaller universe, equipped with the topology generated by finite jointly surjective families. Use sheaves valued in the larger universe. For a scheme $T$ use $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Set $a(S)=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{LC}(S,\mathbf Z)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, where $\operatorname{LC}(S,\mathbf Z)$ is the ring of locally constant integer-valued functions with pointwise operations; continuous maps act by precomposition and then contravariantly by spectrum. Then $a(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is weakly etale, $a$ preserves finite limits as a functor to the pro-etale site, and $a$ sends finite jointly surjective covering families to pro-etale coverings. Left Kan extension along $a^{op}$ followed by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] exists with these universe conventions and defines the inverse image $a^*$ of a geometric morphism. Its abelian-sheaf functor is exact and strong symmetric monoidal for sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

For any scheme $T$ with structure morphism $\pi_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, put $p_T^*=\pi_T^{-1}a^*$ using [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For every scheme morphism $h:T\to U$, the inverse-image composition comparison and $\pi_Uh=\pi_T$ give a canonical monoidal natural isomorphism $h^{-1}p_U^*\cong p_T^*$. These comparisons are compatible with identity morphisms and composition. The corresponding composition comparisons for the abelian inverse images, their lifts to ring and module sheaves, and their termwise functors on derived categories are compatible with identity morphisms and composition. In particular the induced comparison for any commutative square is the one obtained by comparing each composite pullback with the pullback of the common composite scheme morphism.

Normalize condensedPullbackHom using condensedPullbackHom_eq; substitute the structure-map equalities before canceling inverse comparison components. This proves coefficient and abelian coherence. The monoidality of inverse-image comparisons is transported from the monoidal direct-image comparisons by the source CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Conjugate API. Establish its normalization first as an equality of natural transformations, then take components; this avoids expensive component-level iso reductions. Scheme base change is representably flat because it preserves finite limits. Mathlib then gives finite-limit preservation of its opposite left Kan extension and sheafified inverse image. Whiskering with the point inverse image preserves finite limits, and the point composition equation reduces every commutative square to its common composite.

proof.text: Construct the module direct-image identity by Mod.isoMk on lowerStarId and prove uniqueness by faithfulness. Compute the underlying module direct-image composition using the mapMod and comap component formulas. For compatibility with the scalar-extension forgetful isomorphism, use the unit equation for leftAdjointUniq: the extension/restriction unit followed by extendScalarsIsoComapInv has identity underlying map. Expand the composed module adjunction unit to deduce that forgetting it, then applying the pullback comparison, gives the abelian unit. The same equation with the inverse comparison follows by cancellation. For identities, apply unit_conjugateEquiv to both module and abelian identity comparisons; the underlying direct-image identity and injectivity of the abelian adjunction hom equivalence identify their maps. For composition, naturality of the abelian unit and the single-arrow unit equation give the composite unit equation. Apply unit_conjugateEquiv to both composition comparisons and use naturality of lowerStarComp; a generic raw-morphism lemma using the adjunction hom equivalence then gives precisely the requested forgetful compatibility. Existing direct-image unit and associativity arguments conjugate to the module inverse-image coherence, and its normalized square consequence follows by transport and cancellation. No new unproved input is used.
